testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When it is hard to see, like at dawn or dusk, how can a driver make their vehicle more visible?

options.text: Flash the lights on and off.

questions.explanation: Use your headlights on low beam at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather. This helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, if you see fresh oil under your vehicle, this is:
questions.explanation: Check under your vehicle for leaks of oil, coolant, grease, or fuel before driving. Any of these leaks is a problem.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to work?
questions.explanation: Large trucks use air brake systems. These systems use compressed air to operate the brakes.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, cargo weight should be:

options.text: Placed as far left as possible.

questions.explanation: Heavy cargo placed high makes a vehicle more likely to tip over. Keep cargo weight as low as possible to prevent tipping.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: When are people usually the least alert?
questions.explanation: Most drivers are least alert at night, especially after midnight. Fatigue-related crashes happen more often at night than at other times.

questions.question: What is the minimum acceptable tread depth for rear tires?
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth. Rear tires need at least 2/32 of an inch of tread depth. All tires on the same vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, a driver should:

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, use your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo

questions.explanation: Cover cargo to protect people from spills and to protect cargo from weather. Keeping cargo secret is not a reason to cover it.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: Two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
One air brake system with two different sets of controls.
One system for the left side and one for the right side, each with its own controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. One system usually controls the rear brakes and one controls the front brakes.

questions.question: A jogger wearing headphones:

options.text: Is probably aware of what is happening around them.
May not be aware of what is happening around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They cannot hear your vehicle coming and may do something dangerous.

questions.question: Blocking is used to:

options.text: Stop cargo from being loaded too high.
Stop cargo from being unloaded too quickly.

questions.explanation: Blocking is placed in front, behind, and on the sides of cargo to keep it from sliding while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: Do not drive a vehicle if any brake drum has cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check brake drums during your walk-around inspection before driving. It is unsafe to drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not respond to an aggressive driver's angry gestures. Avoid eye contact and do not try to race them.

questions.question: When accelerating on a slippery surface, like a wet road, a driver should:

options.text: Not worry about the road surface.

questions.explanation: Accelerate very gradually when driving on surfaces with poor traction.

questions.question: After an accident, use flares with caution because:

options.text: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares in sunny weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Vehicle fires often happen after accidents when flares are used near spilled fuel. Use flares carefully.

questions.question: To prevent a vehicle from rolling backward when starting to move forward from a stop, you should:
questions.explanation: To prevent a vehicle with manual transmission from rolling backward when starting from a stop, partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.

questions.question: Too much air pressure in a tire:
questions.explanation: Never put too much air pressure in tires. Check your tire air pressure with a gauge during inspections.

questions.question: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) does not need to include which of the following?

options.text: Number of meals eaten by the driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Number of meals eaten by the driver
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include distance traveled, fuel purchased, trip origin, destination, and Vehicle Identification Number. It does not track meals eaten by the driver.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery right after rain begins because:

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Tires are not designed for wet weather.
Water has not yet washed away dirt and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when it first rains. Rainwater creates a slick coating when it mixes with oil and grease that has not yet washed away.

questions.question: A distracted driver:

options.text: Usually follows the rules of the road.
Is a good person to follow.

questions.explanation: Distracted drivers see hazards on the road more slowly than focused drivers. Sometimes they don't see them at all.

questions.question: Friction in an S-cam brake happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction is created when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: When you start a truck with a trailer, your ABS is not working if:

options.text: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the right side of the trailer flashes three times.
All the rear lights flash and then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: Dashboard lights should turn on and then turn off when you start the engine. If the ABS warning light stays on, the system is broken. On a truck with a trailer, if the yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on, the system is not working.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is always dangerous because you may not be able to see everything behind you. Avoid backing whenever possible.

questions.question: How far will an air brake-equipped vehicle need to stop from 55 mph under ideal conditions?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes time to see the danger, time to react, brake lag, and actual braking. An air brake vehicle going 55 mph under ideal conditions needs about 450 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in an air brake system is releasing air:

options.text: You should not be concerned because this is normal.
Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air only if air pressure gets too high. If this valve releases air, something is broken. Have a mechanic fix it.

questions.question: When going down a hill, you can reduce brake use by:
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, slow down and shift to a lower gear. This lets you control your speed without using the brakes too much. Too much braking downhill can overheat your brakes and weaken them.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in ____ seconds.
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, wait for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems. This takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle unattended:

options.text: Lower the windows in the cab.

questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: People working on a disabled vehicle:

options.text: Are probably aware of traffic around them.
May focus on the repair and not notice traffic.
Don't have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: May focus on the repair and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on a broken-down vehicle on the roadside. They may be focused on the repair and not paying attention to traffic.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system:

options.text: Can let poisonous fumes into the cabin.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can let poisonous fumes into the cabin.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can let poisonous fumes into your vehicle. Check your exhaust system regularly for loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: If a driver has stopped on the road and is placing warning triangles:

options.text: Hold the triangles between yourself and oncoming traffic.
Carry the triangles behind your back so other drivers cannot see them until they are placed.
Hold the triangles as low as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the triangles between yourself and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: For your safety, carry warning triangles between your body and the oncoming traffic when placing them.

questions.question: If involved in an accident, a truck driver should:

options.text: Exchange information with all others involved in the accident.
Use a drone to take pictures of the accident scene.
Drive immediately to the nearest police station to file a report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exchange information with all others involved in the accident.
questions.explanation: Stop immediately after an accident to help the injured and exchange information with everyone involved. File a report with law enforcement within four days if anyone is injured or damage is more than $1,000.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle unattended:

options.text: Use the parking brake only if the vehicle is parked on a slope.
Do not use the parking brake, as it can damage the tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when parking your vehicle. However, do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of driver fatigue?
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering recent miles, missing exits or signs, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following vehicles too closely, hitting shoulder rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: Air pressure should build up in a single air system within:
questions.explanation: In single air systems, air pressure should build from about 50 to 90 psi within three minutes.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle controls skills test, your vehicle's final position should be:

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact final position the examiner described.
Within three feet of the final position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact final position the examiner described.
questions.explanation: You must finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position the examiner described. You may fail the basic control skills test if you do not complete an exercise exactly as described.

questions.question: When making tight maneuvers, a driver should:

options.text: Open their door for a better view.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. Check them especially when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact to communicate better.
Stay in their path of travel.

questions.explanation: Get out of an aggressive driver's way if possible. Do not make eye contact, as this could provoke them. Do not let them upset you with their actions.

questions.question: Poor weight balance in a trailer:
questions.explanation: Poorly balanced weight in a trailer makes handling unsafe. Too little or too much weight on the front axle makes steering difficult. Distribute weight evenly from front to back and side to side. Keep weight as low as possible.

questions.question: A driver should make sure that:

options.text: Most cargo is in the front of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Proper loading is critical for safe operation. Bad loading affects how the vehicle handles and can damage it. Loose cargo can also fall off and hurt or kill people.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a concern because it is stopped.
Is only a concern if you see passengers getting off.
Is a concern whether or not you see passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a concern whether or not you see passengers.
questions.explanation: Always be careful near a stopped bus. Passengers may be nearby. The bus may block your view or their view of you.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher on a fire, you should:

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stay as far from the fire as possible.
Point the extinguisher at the top of the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: Stay as far from the fire as possible when using a fire extinguisher. Aim at the base of the fire, not the flames. If you are unsure about the type of fire or what extinguisher to use, wait for firefighters.

questions.question: Which is NOT a cause of hydraulic brake failure?

options.text: Brake fade from overuse on long hills

questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure usually happens for two reasons: loss of hydraulic pressure or overuse on long hills, which causes brake fade.

questions.question: What is the left lane rule?

options.text: Heavy vehicles must only use the left lane on a three-lane road.
Heavy vehicles may only use the left lane on a three-lane road when turning left.
Heavy vehicles cannot use the left lane on a three-lane road for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy vehicles may only use the left lane on a three-lane road when turning left.
questions.explanation: Washington State's left lane rule says vehicles weighing over 10,000 pounds cannot use the left lane on roads with three or more lanes in one direction, except when turning left.

questions.question: A truck tractor built after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: You should ____ if the low pressure warning signal turns on while driving.

options.text: Stop right where you are and park
Leave the roadway safely as soon as possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the roadway safely as soon as possible
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning signal turns on while driving, safely leave the roadway as soon as you can and park. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Yawning a lot or rubbing your eyes

questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, or heavy eyelids; yawning or rubbing eyes; daydreaming; trouble remembering the last few miles; missing exits or signs; trouble holding your head up; drifting from your lane; following too close; hitting shoulder rumble strips; or feeling restless and irritable.

questions.question: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) does NOT need to include which of the following?
questions.explanation: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) must include the distance traveled and fuel purchased. It must show the trip dates and total distance traveled.

questions.question: If an unusual noise or feeling happens in a vehicle while driving, the driver should:

options.text: Hope the vehicle is fine until another driver takes over.
Check it to find the right solution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check it to find the right solution.
questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, have it checked out.
